newsitem.title: USA: Texas lawyer indicted for soliciting crash victims.
newsitem.headline: Texas lawyer indicted for soliciting crash victims.

text.p: One of the country's most successful personal injury lawyers was indicted Thursday for allegedly soliciting clients after a 1994 USAir crash in North Carolina that killed 37 people.

Houston lawyer John O'Quinn was charged with conspiracy with attorneys Charles Benton Musselwhite Sr. and Carl Shaw for alleged improper solicitation of business from families of four victims of the July 1994 crash of USAir Flight 1016.

South Carolina Attorney General Charles Condon said indictments were returned by a grand jury against the lawyers for allegedly hiring "runners" to recruit clients after the plane crashed during a thunderstorm near Charlotte, N.C.
O'Quinn also was charged with offering to split fees with non-lawyers and soliciting clients in South Carolina without being admitted to practice law in the state, prosecutors said.
A fourth attorney, Charles Benton Musselwhite Jr., was charged with one count of solicitation.
The State Bar of Texas is investigating similar allegations, which O'Quinn has denied.
